english.html: rst Emperor of Constantinople, having been killed by the Greeks in battle (where nevertheless it was never possible to find the body, whereby many thought that he was still alive), a little afterwards a pilgrim presented himself in Flanders who resembled the late count Baldwin so well, and moreover had I know not what natural charm which won the hearts of everyone, even so that he gave such good and true tokens, that the greater part constantly maintained that he was the true count Baldwin, and as such several towns received him. But Jeanne, the count's daughter (who commanded at that time in Flanders as heiress of her father), would never recognise him as father, nor receive him as count, and asked counsel, aid and succour of King Louis VIII her uncle; who, curious to learn the truth more closely, summoned him to come to Péronne, where the king at the first meeting was greatly astonished, seeing him wholly like the late count; but remembering that Philip Augustus his father had conferred the order upon the same count, he approached him more closely, asking him the day, the place, and how he had been made knight of the order, and where he had first betrothed his wife. Whereupon this false Baldwin, seeing himself caught, asked for a delay to answer, which was granted him; and by that (and a little afterwards his fraud being still better discovered) he was found in a tavern, and a little afterwards hanged <sup class="mk" data-key="y">y</sup>. Further, I am not ignorant that there have been some in the past who, at the discovery of the deed or a little before, being overtaken by death, have escaped the cruelty of the penalties which Justice would justly have prepared for them: as Joan the Englishwoman, who, dressed as a man and conducted to Athens by a scholar who kept her, profited so much in letters, especially the sacred, that being back in Rome she found no equal, whether in learnedly interpreting and lecturing, or in subtly disputing; whereupon, accompanied by an infinity of graces with which a prodigal heaven had favoured her, and esteemed by all men, she gained so much opinion and authority with the people, singularly with the greatest, that after the death of Pope Leo III she was elected by the consent of all the Romans

notes.citation: Paolo Emili (Paulus Aemilius of Verona), De rebus gestis Francorum, book 7
notes.original: Paule Aemi le, au vij. de re bus geſtis Frã corum.
notes.gloss: The false Baldwin of Flanders, 1225, unmasked by Louis VIII at Péronne and hanged; see the case file §7.

lines: mier Empereur de Conſtantinople, tué des Grecs en
bataille, (ou toutesfois ne fut onc poſſible trouuer le
corps: dont pluſieurs penſoyent qu'il fuſt encore en vie
peu apres ſe preſentant vn pelerin en Flandres, reſſem-
bloit ſi bien au feu comte Balduin: & en outre auoit
ie ne ſçay quel charme naturel, qui gaignoit les cœurs
d'vn chacun: meſmes qu'il donnoi ſi bonnes & verita-
bles enſeignes, que la plus part ſouſtenoient conſtam-
ment, que c'eſtoit le vray comte Balduin, & comme tel
pluſieurs villes le receurent. Mais Ieanne, fille du com-
te (qui commandoit de ce temps- la comme heritiere
du pere en Flandres) ne le voulut oncques recognoi-
ſtre pour pere, ni receuoir pour comte. & demanda con
ſeil, aide, & ſecours au roy Loys viij. ſon oncle. lequel
curieux d'entendre de plus pres la verité, le manda ve-
nir à Peronne, ou le roy fut de premiere rencontre fort
eſtonné, le voyant du tout ſemblable au feu cõte. mais
ſe ſouuenant, que Philippes Auguſte ſon pere auoit
donné l'ordre à iceluy comte, l'accoſta de plus pres, luy
demandant le iour, le lieu, & comment il fut fait che-
ualier de l'ordre, & ou il auoit premierement fiancé ſa
femme. A quoy ce faux Balduin le voyãt prins, deman-
da delay pour reſpondre: qui luy fut ottroye. & par là
(& peu apres encore mieux ſa fraude deſcouuerte) fut
trouué dans vn cabaret, & peu apres pendu {y}. D'auanta
ge ie n'ignore pas qu'il n'en y ayt eu quelques vns par
le paſſé, qui ſur la deſcouuerte du faict, ou peu deuant,
ſurprins de la mort, ont euité la cruauté des peines que
Iuſtice leur euſt iuſtement preparees: comme Ieanne
l'Angloiſe, laquelle accouſtrée en homme, & condui-
re en Athenes par vn eſcolier, qui l'entretenoit, prou-
fita tellement aux lettres, meſmement aux ſainctes,
qu'eſtant de retour à Rome, ne trouuoit pareil: fuſt
à doctement interpreter, & lire, ou a ſubtilement
diſputer. dont elle accompagnée d'vne infinité de
graces, deſquelles le ciel prodigue l'auoit fauoriſée,
& eſtimée de tous hommes, gaigna tant d'opinion,
& authorité enuers le peuple, ſingulierement à l'en-
droit des plus grans, qu'apres la mort du Pape Leon
iij. fut eſleuë du conſentement de tous. Les Romains
Paule Aemi
le, au vij. de re
bus geſtis Frã
corum.
